[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance document defines the enterprise design token taxonomy, Tailwind CSS CSS variable integration strategy, dark mode approach, and tenant branding extension points for all React-based frontend applications at Gainwell Technologies.

Design tokens are the single source of truth for all visual decisions — colors, typography, spacing, radius, shadows — across the enterprise design system. By expressing tokens as CSS custom properties consumed by Tailwind CSS, the enterprise achieves consistent theming across products, automated WCAG 2.2 contrast validation, and tenant-specific branding without forking the design system.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

Following this guidance ensures:

- **Visual consistency**: All product UIs use the same color palette, type scale, and spacing — reducing per-product design decisions
- **WCAG 2.2 compliance from the token layer**: Contrast ratios are validated at token definition, not retrofitted per component
- **Tenant branding without forking**: State agencies and health plans override only their brand tokens; the design system remains unified
- **Dark mode support**: A semantic token layer means dark mode is a CSS variable swap — no duplicate component styles required
- **Token documentation**: A centralized token taxonomy means design, engineering, and accessibility teams share a common vocabulary

[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The enterprise UI component stack (ADR-APP-003) mandates Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS. Shadcn/UI generates components that reference Tailwind CSS utility classes backed by CSS custom properties defined in `globals.css`. Without a centralized token taxonomy, teams define these CSS variables independently, producing color palette drift across products, unvalidated contrast ratios, and conflicting dark mode implementations.

Multi-tenant deployments (PTN-APP-MTN-013) require per-tenant brand customization — state agency colors, logos, and typography — without creating design system forks. The design token layer is the mechanism that enables this: tenants override only their brand tokens; all structural and semantic tokens remain shared.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Tailwind CSS maps utility classes (e.g., `bg-primary`, `text-foreground`) to CSS custom properties (e.g., `--primary`, `--foreground`) defined in `globals.css`. This indirection is the key insight: changing the CSS custom property value changes the visual output of every component that uses the corresponding utility class — without modifying component code.

Shadcn/UI's `init` command generates a default token set. This guidance standardizes and extends that token set for the enterprise.

[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#design-token-taxonomy]

### Design Token Taxonomy

**The canonical source of truth for all enterprise design tokens is `@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css`.** This stylesheet is published as part of `mmes-cmn-core` and is imported once by the host shell. All product module CSS consumes its tokens directly. Portal Studio overrides them at the tenant level at runtime.

The token taxonomy has three layers:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Layer 3: Component-Sizing Constants                              │
│  e.g. --widget-input-height, --button-height, --font-size-regular │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Layer 2: Semantic Tokens (role-based, theme-switched)            │
│  e.g. --text-primary, --background-primary, --widget-border       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Layer 1: Primitive Tokens (raw palette — never used directly)    │
│  e.g. --gainwell-blue, --blue-400, --neutral-300, --green-400     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

All layers are defined in `@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css`. Import it once at the host shell level:

```js
import '@mmes/cmn-core/core-theme.css';
```

In local development and test harnesses, import it explicitly from the package or reference it via CDN:
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@mmes/cmn-core/components/react/core-theme.css">
```

[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#wcag-22-contrast-compliance-at-the-token-level]

### WCAG 2.2 Contrast Compliance at the Token Level

All semantic token color pairs must meet WCAG 1.4.3 contrast requirements **before deployment**. Validate token pairs with automated tooling:

| Token Pair                                         | Minimum Ratio | WCAG Criterion |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| `--text-primary` on `--background-primary`         | 4.5:1         | 1.4.3 AA       |
| `--text-inverse` on `--button-bg-primary`          | 4.5:1         | 1.4.3 AA       |
| `--text-error` on `--background-primary`           | 4.5:1         | 1.4.3 AA       |
| `--text-secondary` on `--background-primary`       | 4.5:1         | 1.4.3 AA       |
| `--text-primary` on `--background-primary` (dark)  | 4.5:1         | 1.4.3 AA       |

Contrast validation is incorporated into the STD-APP-UI-001 CI gate.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#adding-a-new-token]

### Adding a New Token

When a new visual decision is needed (e.g., a success state background):

1. **Define the primitive** (if a new color value): Add `--green-100: #eaf6e9;` to the primitive layer in `core-theme.css`
2. **Define the semantic token**: Add `--notification-bg-success: var(--green-100);` to the semantic layer (`:root` and `.theme-light`)
3. **Add the dark mode override**: Add the dark-mode equivalent in the `.theme-dark` block
4. **Map to Tailwind**: Add `'notification-success': 'var(--notification-bg-success)'` to `tailwind.config.ts` colors
5. **Validate contrast**: Run the contrast check for the new token pair
6. **Document**: Update the token taxonomy table in this guidance document
7. **Publish**: The change goes into `@mmes/cmn-core` — all consuming modules inherit it automatically on next import
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#typography-scale]

### Typography Scale

The enterprise typography scale uses **Arial / Poppins Bold** (defined in `core-theme.css`) and maps to Tailwind via `var(--font-size-*)` tokens. Note: `core-theme.css` sets `html { font-size: 62.5% }`, so `1.6rem = 16px`.

| Token                   | Value (rem) | Computed px | Tailwind Class | Usage                         |
| ----------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | -------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `--font-size-xsmall`    | 1.2rem      | 12px        | `text-xs`      | Captions, helper text         |
| `--font-size-small`     | 1.4rem      | 14px        | `text-sm`      | Table cells, secondary labels |
| `--font-size-regular`   | 1.6rem      | 16px        | `text-base`    | Default body (≥16px for WCAG) |
| `--font-size-large`     | 1.8rem      | 18px        | `text-lg`      | Sub-headings                  |
| `--font-size-xlarge`    | 2.2rem      | 22px        | `text-xl`      | Section headings              |
| `--font-size-xxlarge`   | 2.6rem      | 26px        | `text-2xl`     | Page titles                   |
| `--font-size-3xlarge`   | 3.0rem      | 30px        | `text-3xl`     | Hero headings                 |

**Note**: Body text must be ≥16px to satisfy WCAG 1.4.12 (Text Spacing) readability at default zoom.

[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#token-change-control]

### Token Change Control

Design token changes follow a governed process:

1. **Propose**: Token change proposed with contrast validation results
2. **Review**: Architecture and UX review to assess impact across products
3. **Approve**: Enterprise Architecture Practice approves primitive and semantic token changes
4. **Release**: Token changes are versioned and communicated to all consuming teams with a migration window

Tenant brand token overrides do not require enterprise approval but must pass the automated contrast validator in the Tenant Theme Registry (PTN-APP-MTN-013).

[strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md#token-compliance-indicators]

### Token Compliance Indicators

- **Contrast pass rate**: Percentage of semantic token pairs that pass WCAG 1.4.3 (target: 100%)
- **Hardcoded color violations**: Count of `bg-[#...]` or `text-[#...]` usages in production code (target: 0)
- **Token coverage**: Percentage of visual design decisions expressed as tokens vs. ad-hoc values (target: >95%)
- **Dark mode parity**: Percentage of pages/components with verified dark mode rendering (target: 100% for new work)
